entries.en: What's this? One of the Earth-clan? Ah, a very famous one, yes? You are the one called Shepard.
Forgive me, Earth-clan. My name is Barla Von. My job makes it necessary for me to keep informed.
Is there anything I can do for you today, Commander?
Goodbye, Commander.
I don't like strangers keeping tabs on me.
I should go.
Are you spying on me?
Goodbye.
Galactic finance is incredibly complex: a mix of laws and regulations from dozens of interstellar economies.
I'm an expert in how all those economies interact. For a fee, I share my expertise.
I also offer premium services for those clients who need someone to conduct business without drawing unwanted attention. Discreet and efficient. That's my motto.
Everything I do falls completely within the bounds of interstellar commerce law. Even so, many of my clients would prefer their transactions remain undisclosed.
For example, suppose a hanar ambassador was petitioning the Council to reduce tariffs on hanar goods. How would it look if he had money invested in a hanar exporting company?
Even if his true motives were to help his people, he would be accused of advancing the petition for his own personal gain. I can keep his personal finances private.
Then we can only hope you will never be cursed with a large enough fortune to require my services.
Most people think I deal in finances, but my real currency is knowledge. I trade information, and it has made me very wealthy.
But the Shadow Broker is the true master. Every day, he buys and sells secrets that could topple governments, always giving them to the highest bidder.
Yet somehow he never seems to upset the natural balance of power. All those secrets being passed around seem to even out. Nobody ends up with an advantage in the end.
I don't know. Nobody does. The Shadow Broker could be any race, any gender. I have a theory that it's actually an entire group working under one identity.
How else could they juggle so many contacts at the same time? How else could they keep all that information from getting crossed? But they've got the perfect setup.
Every government is forced to play their game so they don't get behind. But no matter how long you play, no matter how many secrets you buy, you can never win.
Greetings, Earth-clan.
I believe congratulations are in order, Commander Shepard. You are the first human to join the Spectres, yes?
One you are no doubt ready for. A word of warning, though. There are many eyes watching you now, Commander. Some of them want to see you fail.
I, however, wish you only success. Perform well and you bring the Earth-clan one step closer to joining the Council.
And if they let your people in, maybe there is hope for my own species one day, yes?
Don't underestimate this opportunity, Commander. You have a chance to do great things for the Earth-clan.
Perform well and your species may soon be asked to join the Council. There is no greater honor in the galaxy. A word of warning, however.
The eyes of the entire galaxy are on you now. Some of them are hoping you will fail. Be careful, Commander.
How can this humble servant be of use to you?
You've got me at a disadvantage here.
Sounds pretty shady.
Still sounds shady to me.
Tell me more about the Shadow Broker.
Any guess what his identity might be?
It's a great honor.
It's no big deal.
Tell me more about your job.
Who are you?
Thank you.
So what?
Personal questions
The Shadow Broker
Is this legal?
I don't buy it.
Who is he?
The tale of how you survived the great tragedy on Akuze is truly remarkable. I am amazed each time I hear it.
No matter what you think of Saren, he's not stupid. He knows the Shadow Broker is a valuable ally.
Turning on him doesn't make sense. Not unless something huge was at stake.
I don't know the details, but the Shadow Broker hired a freelancer to deal with it. A krogan mercenary.
I just told you that the most famous Spectre in the galaxy betrayed the Shadow Broker. Quite a bargain, considering the price.
Speak with the krogan if you want to learn more. I heard he was paying a visit to Citadel Security. If you hurry you might catch him before he leaves the Academy.
Yes. I believe he's the one. I heard he was paying a visit to Citadel Security. If you hurry you might catch him before he leaves the C-Sec Academy.
I heard he was paying Citadel Security a visit. If you hurry you can probably catch him before he leaves the C-Sec Academy.
Very. However, I doubt the visit was entirely his choice. You'll need to speak with him if you want to know more.
My pleasure, Commander.
How can I be of assistance to you today, Earth-clan?
The station is, without a doubt, the greatest wonder in the galaxy. It is a technological marvel. But its true splendor goes much deeper than the hull and engines.
From the Presidium to the wards, the entire station is a testament to the success of the Council. All the species of Citadel space together in a single strong community.
It's the political center of Citadel space. Eighty percent of all intelligent species in the known galaxy acknowledge the Council's authority on interstellar matters.
But only the most powerful and influential species have embassies here on the Presidium. This level of the station is reserved for the elite, Shepard. People like us.
The cultural heart of the galaxy. They pulse with the lifeblood of millions of citizens from dozens of different species.
You never know what you'll find down in the wards, Commander. It's always full of surprises. Fortunately, most of them are pleasant.
From time to time, I come across information I sell to the Shadow Broker. That's my only involvement. I like it that way.
The more you know, the more dangerous the game becomes. I don't like danger, Commander. I'll leave that to you.
It is a great honor to welcome the hero of the Blitz.
You were at Torfan, correct? You led the final assault against the enemy base, if memory serves.
I am a financial advisor to many important clients here on the Citadel. When someone as important as yourself arrives on the station, I take notice.
I am a financial advisor to many important clients here on the Citadel. When someone as important as yourself arrives on the station, I take notice.
You're very blunt, Shepard. And you're right. But Wrex has already told you far more than I know about this. I am sorry, but I have nothing else to offer.
You're very blunt, Shepard. But you're right. I am an agent for the Shadow Broker. And I do know something about Saren.
Normally, this information would cost a small fortune. But these are exceptional circumstances. So I'm going to give it to you for free.
Threats don't work on me, Commander. This information is worth a small fortune. But this is an unusual situation. So I'm going to let you have it for free.
What's the catch?
What's the catch?
What's the catch?
There is no catch. The Shadow Broker is quite upset with Saren right now. They used to do a lot of business. Until Saren turned on him.
I think I know him. His name's Wrex.
How do I find him?
Isn't it strange that a krogan would want to speak with C-Sec?
Thanks for the info.
What's it like living here on the Citadel?
What makes the Presidium so special?
What are the wards like?
I thought you'd know more about the man you work for.
I heard you work for the Shadow Broker. Do you have any information about Saren?
I hear your information can be expensive.
I need that information. Now.
That's what happens when you deal with a traitor like Saren.
Saren betrayed him. Imagine that.
Saren's turned on a lot of people lately.
That's not much to go on.
Have we met?
Have we met?
Have we met?
I need your help.
I need information.
I need your help.
I need information.
I was told to talk to you.
Can we make a deal?
What's the cost?
Start talking.
Serves him right.
What a shock.
He's not the only one.
Anything else?
Wrex?
Where is he?
Why is he there?
Let's go.
The Citadel
Tell me about the Presidium.
Tell me about the wards.
But you're his agent.
I'm sure there will be some type of catch.
Ah, human. This one is greatly pleased to see you here in my decadent Emporium.
Please take time to examine the fine goods it has for purchase, all of great worth.
Only the finest and most luxurious items that credits can buy.
This one is able to procure almost any item the human would desire. For a price, naturally.
Oh, this one is pleased to do so, human. You will not be disappointed.
For the same reason that humans are so inquisitive. It is part of our culture.
Specifically, hanar only refer to themselves in the first person with family or intimates.
Return soon. This one receives new shipments regularly.
Human Commander, it is pleasing to see you again. This one has received some outstanding new items since it last saw the other.
Commander, it is good to see you again. Would you care to see some of its fantastic items today?
What exactly do you sell?
I'd like to see these rare and wonderful items.
I think I should be going.
Show me your items.
Why do you refer to yourself as "this one" and "it"?
I think I'll be going.
Goods
I'd like to buy something.
Your speech
No, thanks.
Let's see what you have.
Goodbye.
Human Commander, this one has received some magnificent new items since it last saw the other.
Human Commander. This one has received some fabulous new items since it last saw the other.
This one's face name is Delanynder, though many in this place simply refer to it as Delan.
And we rarely do so with other species. It is just our way.
A shop. Many wonderful items for sale.
As you wish. Do return when you are able.
Who are you?
What is that?
I should be going.
Personal question
Emporium
So long.

Looks like another relay. As best I can tell, the receiver for the new signal is somewhere on the Presidium.
Another relay! Whoever it is, they're somewhere on the Presidium.
Another relay! Whoever it is, they're somewhere on the Presidium.
